reasons.A: Closest sentence movement: short declaratives set against long semicoloned ones, 'For'/'Nor' openings, generic 'he'/'the man', dashed asides and a paradoxical assertive stance, all in the passage's measured period diction.
reasons.B: Period register and dashes fit, and the rhetorical question echoes the author, but sentences run longer and more evenly, and the closing 'I suspect' hedges where the author asserts.
reasons.C: Modern, first-person, confiding essay voice ('What interests me', 'I think this is worth holding on to'), with plain diction and few of the author's semicolon-and-dash rhythms.
